question: Do pairwise role-preserving rewrites compose into transitive functional-identity classes whose previously unpaired multi-hop members remain topology-coherent?

identityConstruction.candidateIdentityClass: connected component of legal edges within one lane
identityConstruction.compositionTarget: pair of observations in the same legal component connected by at least two legal edges and not themselves a direct legal edge
identityConstruction.consistencyFalsifier: any already-scored broken pair whose endpoints fall inside one legal connected component

normalization: Counts except centerCount are divided by centerCount; train observations alone define feature means and population standard deviations.
comparison: Within each lane and physical-family-pair stratum, compare topology distance of multi-hop same-component pairs against cross-component pairs with the same physical-family pair. Smaller same-component distance is positive evidence. Equal-weight family-pair effects are averaged.
falsifier: If legal edges do not compose transitively in an independent lane, or multi-hop members are not more topology-coherent than family-matched cross-component controls, functional identity is not supported as an equivalence class under these rewrites.
claimBoundary: This tests transitive composition of already-frozen role-preserving relations. It does not prove that every member of a component has identical semantics or that all legal rewrites have been discovered.
